factor_recurrence_regularization.concept: what would make it a theorem
factor_recurrence_regularization.equation: regularizer certificate + factor map q + recurrence/separation certificate + quantitative bound
factor_recurrence_regularization.status: requires an explicit theorem linking the chosen regularizer to a recurrence, contraction, invariance, quotient stability, or generalization bound

factor_recurrence_regularization.equation: (N,+,·) -> regularized parameter dynamics -> bounded/stable factor image -> finite-factor recurrence
factor_recurrence_regularization.status: candidate graphable route, not a repository theorem
factor_recurrence_regularization.condition: Nat is algebraically unbounded, so recurrence does not follow from the semiring alone. A separate regularizer or invariant-set certificate must bound the observed factor trajectory or make it finite.
factor_recurrence_regularization.generalization_link: If the regularizer also yields algorithmic stability, contraction, or controlled hypothesis-class complexity, a separate generalization bound can be composed with factor recurrence. Recurrence itself is not a generalization guarantee.

reason: The repository has the connected composition surfaces and factor-recurrence mechanism, but it does not yet contain the strict nonrepresentability witness needed for a neural function-class separation, nor a theorem proving that a specific regularizer mathematically forces or predicts factor recurrence.
no_invention_policy: Do not invent a new exotic theorem merely to complete the graph. Existing pre-graphed theorem surfaces are used first; new theorem promotion requires an actual Agda proposition.

promotion_policy.rule: Disconnected component theorems are not separation nodes. They are promoted into the smallest existing composed theorem that already packages their semantics, and the strict graph retains only the single full connected composition.
promotion_policy.note: These records remain on the Agda proof surface and may remain required CI declarations; exclusion here means they are not treated as independent function-class separation claims.

future_theorem_policy.rule: Every future theorem enters the strict separation graph only through an existing fully connected composition node. A disconnected theorem may be retained on the Agda/CI surface, but it is not a function-class separation claim until a composed theorem consumes its semantics.

required_witnesses.inclusion: An explicit Agda term proving F_base subseteq F_full_connected under the same input/output semantics and resource convention.
required_witnesses.membership: An explicit Agda witness f together with a proof f in F_full_connected that traverses the full connected composition.
required_witnesses.nonrepresentability: An explicit Agda proof f notin F_base; naming a candidate witness without this proof does not establish separation.

future_admission_gate: theorem_graph_search discovers a path through the full connected composition
the inclusion and nonrepresentability witness obligations are discharged
only then may status change from NOT_ESTABLISHED to SEPARATED
